question.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12}{x}-3{x}^{2})}{(3+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{0-3{x}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-{x}^{2}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
